DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OILG OPINION NO. ATTY. ALFIE JAY O. NIQUIA Room 3, 2nd Fir, D.E and T Bldg., Villavert st San Jose Antique alfeniquia@gmail.com Dear Atty. Niquia: This has reference to your Letter dated June 18, 2025 seeking guidance as to whether the suspended Antique Sangguniang Panlalawigan Members who won during the May 2025 elections may assume office on June 30, 2025. In your Letter, you narrated that the following Antique Sangguniang Panlalawigan Members were suspended by the Office of the Ombudsman for one (1) year and, together with SPM Victor R. Condez, were elected/re-elected into public office during the May 2025 elections. You also inquired whether Julius Cezar O. Tajanlangit (Liga ng mga Barangay Provincial Federation President/Ex Officio SPM) and Kenneth Dave B. Gasalao (Sangguniang Kabataan Provincial Federation President/Ex Officio Member), may assume office on June 30, 2025 despite the one (I) year Ombudsman suspension. You stated your position that (I) Sec. 66(b) of the Local Government Code (LGC) provides that the duration of the penalty of suspension should not extend beyond the unexpired term of the public official; (2) that the case of Pascual vs. Provincial Board of Nueva Ecijal states that an officer cannot be suspended for a misconduct committed during a prior term; and (3) you have a pending petition for review on certiorari with application for the issuance of a temporary restraining order and/or writ of preliminary injunction before the Court of Appeals. We respectfully differ. First, Sec. 66(b)2 of the LGC should be read in conjunction with Sec. 613 which G.R. No. L-11959. 31 October 1959. 2 Section 62. Notice of hearing. - (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the offce. 3 Section 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective offcial shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President; "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

identifies the proper disciplining authority over complaints against local elective officials. Thus, the provision on suspensions not exceeding the unexpired term only applies to orders issues by the disciplining authorities mentioned under Sec. 61 Moreover, the authority of the Office of the Ombudsman to impose suspension orders is not anchoæd on the LGC but rather, Sec. 25 of R A, No. 6770. Sec. 254 does not contain a provision on the service of suspension. Based on the foregoing, we are of the view that Sec. 66(b) does not apply to suspension orders issued by the Office of the Ombudsman and any suspension order issued by it prior to the 90-day period shall remain in effect. Second, as regards your pending petition before the Court of Appeals, in a plethora of cases, the Supreme Court has consistently upheld the principle that administrative penalties imposed by the Ombudsman are self-executory and are not suspended by the mere filing of an appeal or application for injunctive writ. The pronouncement in DILG v. Gatuz5, is particularly instructive and resolute. There, the Highest Court unequivocally declared that "decisions of the Ombudsman in disciplinary cases are immediately executory and cannot be stayed by the filing of an appeal or the issuance of an injunctive writ. " Lastly, the case of Pascual vs. Provincial Board of Nueva Ecija6 wherein the condonation doctrine originated, is no longer controlling. In Carpio Morales v. CAI the Supreme Court ruled that the condonation doctrine is not based on statutory law but a mere jurisprudential creation, viz: 'To begin with, the concept of public office is a public trust and the corollary requirement of accountability to the people at all times, as mandated under the 1987 Constitution, is plainly inconsistent with the idea that an elective local official's administrative liability for a misconduct committed during a prior term can be wiped off by the fact that he was elected to a second term of office, or even another elective post. Election is not a mode of condoning an administrative offense, and there is simply no constitutional or statutory basis in our jurisdiction to support the notion that an official elected for a different term is fully absolved of any administrative liability arising from an offense done during a prior term. (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the sangguniang panlalawjgan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A cornplaint against any elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguntang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory. Section 25. Penalties. - (1 ) In adrrumstrative proceedings under Presidential Decree NO. 807 , the penalties and rules provided therein shall be applied. No. 191176. October 14, 2016. G.R. No. L-11959, 31 October 1959 G.R. Nos. 217126-27, November 10, 2015.

xxx Relatedly it should be clarified that thoro is no truth in Pascual's postulation that tho courts would bo depriving the electorate of their right to elect their officers if condonation were not to be sanctioned. In political law, election portains to the process by which a particular constituency chooses an individual to hold a public office. In this junsdiction, there is, again, no legal basis to conclude that election automatically implies condonation. Neither is there any legal basis to say that every democratic and republican state has an inherent regime of condonation. If condonation of an elective official's administrative liability would perhaps, be allowed in this jurisdiction, then the same should have been provided by law under our goveming legal mechanisms. May it be at the time of Pascual or at present, by no means has it been shown that such a law, whether in a constitutional or statutory provision, exists. Therefore, infeming from this manifest absence, it cannot be said that the electorate's will has been abdicated " Based on the foregoing, the Department is of the view that you may not assume on June 30, 2025 and thereafter until the penalty of one (I) year suspension is fully served. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs JUAN JOVIAN INGENIERO, CESO III ReÄd Diredor.
